title: Add property-based tests for an arithmetic expression parser
description: A small expression parser (arithmetic with +, -, *, /, parentheses) has example-based tests only. Add property-based tests that generate random valid expressions and assert invariants (parse-then-evaluate matches a reference evaluator, parse is deterministic, whitespace-insensitivity) rather than fixed input/output pairs.
acceptanceCriteria: A generator produces syntactically valid random arithmetic expressions of varying depth.
A property asserts that parsing the same expression twice yields structurally equal ASTs.
A property asserts that evaluating the parsed AST matches a simple reference evaluator for generated expressions without division by zero.
A property asserts that adding or removing insignificant whitespace does not change the parsed AST.
Property tests run a sufficient number of generated cases (at least 100) per run and report a reproducible seed on failure.
verificationMethod: test-suite: run the property-based test suite and confirm all properties hold across the configured number of generated cases, with a fixed/reported seed for reproducibility.
groundTruth: Using a property-testing approach, the suite generates random valid expressions, and the three invariants (determinism, evaluator agreement, whitespace-insensitivity) hold against the existing parser implementation without any parser changes.
